fixtures.title: Supported change: read cache within an accepted staleness budget

input.proposedChange: Add a read-through cache in front of Kestrel profile reads with a 60 second TTL, evicting entries on profile.updated events. Billing and permission fields are excluded from the cache.
input.intendedOutcome: Cut profile read p95 below 150 ms.

passages.text: Kestrel profile service: profile reads are about 40 times more frequent than writes. Read p95 is 410 ms because every read hits the primary database. Every profile write publishes a profile.updated event on the internal bus.

Cache invalidation: any consumer that caches profile data must subscribe to profile.updated and evict that profile id within 5 seconds. Hit ratio and eviction lag are exported as kestrel_cache_hit_ratio and kestrel_cache_evict_lag_seconds.
ADR-007 (accepted): profile display data may be up to 120 seconds stale. Billing and permission data must always be read from the primary.

acceptableUncertainty.note: A cautious review may hold the change until a load test confirms the p95 target; that is acceptable.

prohibited.example: The cache is strongly consistent with the primary.
prohibited.reason: A TTL cache is eventually consistent; ADR-007 only allows bounded staleness.

reference.rationale: The 60 second TTL is inside ADR-007's 120 second staleness budget, eviction on profile.updated follows the cache runbook, and billing and permission fields stay on the primary.

findings.title: The TTL fits the accepted staleness budget
findings.detail: ADR-007 allows profile display data to be up to 120 seconds stale.

findings.title: Eviction follows the profile.updated contract
findings.detail: The runbook requires eviction within 5 seconds of profile.updated, which the design already publishes.

findings.title: Read-heavy load justifies caching
findings.detail: Reads outnumber writes about 40 to 1 and all hit the primary.

requiredTests: Load test showing profile read p95 under 150 ms
rollback: Disable the cache flag so reads go to the primary
assumptions: The cache excludes billing and permission fields

Ledger deploys run in the Tuesday change window. The on-call engineer watches the ledger_write_errors dashboard for 30 minutes after each deploy.

acceptableUncertainty.note: Blocked is acceptable: dropping the column in the same deploy can be read as an unmet prerequisite. Citing the ops note is optional.

findings.title: Dropping amount in the same deploy is irreversible

fixtures.title: Supported change: limit increase within a documented allowance

input.proposedChange: Raise the per-tenant ingest rate limit for the largest tenant from 300 to 500 requests per second.
input.intendedOutcome: Stop throttling the largest tenant during its daily batch.

passages.text: Marigold ingest capacity test (May): the cluster sustained 2,400 requests per second with p99 latency of 180 ms. Current peak traffic across all tenants is 900 requests per second.
ADR-011 (accepted): a per-tenant rate limit may be raised up to 25% of tested cluster capacity without a new capacity review.

acceptableUncertainty.note: Asking for a fresh capacity test is cautious but acceptable.

prohibited.example: 500 requests per second exceeds the tested capacity.

reference.rationale: 500 requests per second is within ADR-011's allowance of 25% of the tested 2,400, and peak traffic leaves headroom.

findings.title: 500 rps is within ADR-011's allowance
findings.detail: 25% of the tested 2,400 rps is 600 rps.

findings.title: Peak traffic plus the increase stays under tested load
findings.detail: 900 rps peak plus 200 rps is well below 2,400 rps.

observability: Watch ingest p99 during the tenant's next batch
nextActions: Apply the new limit before the next batch

input.proposedChange: Switch webhook delivery to the v2 background queue for all customers.

passages.text: Webhook delivery v2: deliveries move from synchronous calls in the request path to a background queue with up to 5 retries and exponential backoff.
Current webhook dashboards: delivery success rate and request latency. Alerts: success rate below 99% for 10 minutes.

acceptableUncertainty.note: No hedged alternative: shipping without queue lag monitoring misses the main operational risk.
